preconditions.expression: t == int(stdin.split()[0]) and t >= 1 and t <= 10**5
preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^5) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 10**5 for n in [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::3]])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line after t is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) representing the length of the permutations.

preconditions.expression: all(len(a) == n and set(a) == set(range(1, n+1)) for a in [list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::3]])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second line after n is a permutation a of length n with distinct integers from 1 to n.

preconditions.expression: all(len(b) == n and set(b) == set(range(1, n+1)) for b in [list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[3::3]])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the third line after n is a permutation b of length n with distinct integers from 1 to n.

preconditions.expression: all(len(d) == n and all(di == 0 or di == a[i] or di == b[i] for i, di in enumerate(list(map(int, line.split())))) for a, d in zip([list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::3]], [list(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[4::3]]))
preconditions.description: For each test case, the fourth line after n is a list d of length n where each element is either 0, a[i], or b[i], indicating known values of c.
The input is well-formed with exactly 4 lines per test case (n, a, b, d) and a leading t line.

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout.split()) == t and all(0 <= int(out) < 10**9 + 7 for out in stdout.split()))
postconditions.description: The output contains exactly t integers, one per test case, each representing the number of valid permutations c modulo 10^9 + 7.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(out) <= 2**n for out in stdout.split())
postconditions.description: Each output integer is a non-negative count of valid permutations c, modulo 10^9 + 7.

postconditions.expression: all(any(all(c[i] == a[i] or c[i] == b[i] for i in range(n)) and set(c) == set(range(1, n+1)) and all(c[i] == d[i] if d[i] != 0 else True for i in range(n)) for c in [list(map(int, line.split())) for line in [stdin.splitlines()[i] for i in range(4, 4*t+1, 4)]]) if any(all(c[i] == a[i] or c[i] == b[i] for i in range(n)) and set(c) == set(range(1, n+1)) and all(c[i] == d[i] if d[i] != 0 else True for i in range(n)) for c in [list(map(int, line.split())) for line in [stdin.splitlines()[i] for i in range(4, 4*t+1, 4)]]))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output count is the number of permutations c where: (1) each c[i] is either a[i] or b[i], (2) c is a permutation of 1..n, and (3) c[i] == d[i] for all i where d[i] != 0. The count is modulo 10^9 + 7.
